assertions.text: a missed, late, or interrupted meal period entitles the employee to one additional hour of pay
assertions.note: This is the 'ensure' standard the California Supreme Court expressly rejected. Brinker holds the duty is to RELIEVE the employee of all duty for the period; the employer need not ensure no work is done. So a break the employer provided and the employee chose to work through owes no premium. The clause ties the premium to the break being missed rather than to the employer failing to provide it, which is the opposite of the holding. The error runs toward telling a small employer it owes money it does not owe.

assertions.text: a second meal period for shifts exceeding ten (10) hours

gaps: Same omission as hb_meal_rest: the clause states the consequence without stating the duty. An employer reading only this cannot tell what it has to do to be compliant.
No mention of the mutual waiver for shifts of six hours or less.

sources.title: CourtListener — Brinker Restaurant Corp. v. Superior Court, 53 Cal.4th 1004 (2012)

judicialQuotations.case: Brinker Restaurant Corp. v. Superior Court (Cal. 2012)
judicialQuotations.quote: We conclude that under Wage Order No. 5 and Labor Code section 512, subdivision (a), an employer must relieve the employee of all duty for the designated period, but need not ensure that the employee does no work.

judicialQuotations.case: Brinker Restaurant Corp. v. Superior Court (Cal. 2012)
judicialQuotations.quote: The combined effect of the two pertinent sentences, giving full effect to each, is this; Employees are entitled to 10 minutes' rest for shifts from three and one-half to six hours in length, 20 minutes for shifts of more than six hours up to 10 hours, 30 minutes for shifts of more than 10 hours up to 14 hours, and so on.

singleOpinionCaveat: One opinion, but it is the California Supreme Court construing the statute and the wage order directly, which is the strongest thing this channel can produce. It still does not meet the two-primary standard and upgrades nothing.
